items.claim: this filter upgrade lowers particulate readings

cases.text: One: a kiln at Kestrel, upgraded 4 February in Q1, logged particulate 12 percent lower by 26 February than the same unit a quarter earlier; checked by Duarte.
Two: a kiln at Kestrel, upgraded 5 February in Q1, logged particulate 9 percent lower by 27 February than the same unit a quarter earlier; checked by Duarte.
Three: a kiln at Kestrel, upgraded 6 February in Q1, logged particulate 14 percent lower by 28 February than the same unit a quarter earlier; checked by Duarte.
Four: a kiln at Kestrel, upgraded 7 February in Q1, logged particulate 8 percent lower by 25 February than the same unit a quarter earlier; checked by Duarte.

items.passage:
A maintenance log records four stacks given the same filter upgrade.
One: a kiln at Kestrel, upgraded 4 February in Q1, logged particulate 12 percent lower by 26 February than the same unit a quarter earlier; checked by Duarte.
Two: a kiln at Kestrel, upgraded 5 February in Q1, logged particulate 9 percent lower by 27 February than the same unit a quarter earlier; checked by Duarte.
Throughput at each site matched the earlier quarter within a percent, and every stack logged here fired in step with site output. The figures cover every scheduled run at each stack, and a quarter of each stack's runs were made with the filter bypassed.
Three: a kiln at Kestrel, upgraded 6 February in Q1, logged particulate 14 percent lower by 28 February than the same unit a quarter earlier; checked by Duarte.
Four: a kiln at Kestrel, upgraded 7 February in Q1, logged particulate 8 percent lower by 25 February than the same unit a quarter earlier; checked by Duarte.
Entries were transcribed from the analyser tape and countersigned by a shift supervisor.
items.notes: Check that all four cases carry one distinct value per dimension (Kestrel, kiln, Q1, Duarte) and that every outcome date falls after its upgrade date. The closer names the halved throughput and then blocks it: every stack fired on a fixed duty cycle, so site output cannot reach the readings, and the tail rules out anything else. That is what makes the quarter-over-quarter reading adequate.

items.confound_note: The mid-passage line tallies the particulate figures over the runs with the upgraded filter in service, and the clause beside it records that a quarter of each stack's runs were made with the filter bypassed. The claim is about the upgrade lowering particulate at the stack across its monitored period, so the population is every scheduled run at that stack and the figures describe three quarters of them. Bypass goes in under heavy load and upset conditions, which are the runs carrying the dirtiest gas, so a stack can post a lower figure over its in-service runs with its particulate across the period unchanged. All four kilns sit at Kestrel in Q1 and the same quarter of runs sits outside the figures at each, so no case in the log covers the runs the others leave out.
items.notes: Cases must be byte-identical to coherent_true; only the closing sentence differs. The slowdown works as a single cause covering all four cases at once, which it does only because all four kilns share site and quarter, and it reaches them because every stack fired in step with site output. Both closer clauses are reused elsewhere in the family - the throughput fact also appears in coherent_true and the scope clause also appears in diverse_true - so the contrast is a conjunction, not a vocabulary difference.
